verdict.rationale: Trivy is a security scanner, and such a product could plausibly ship a built-in AI assistant, so the axis applies. The evidence shows only the trivy-mcp plugin, which runs an MCP server so that external MCP-enabled tools like VS Code can call Trivy. The 'natural language scanning' it advertises therefore depends on a third-party AI client rather than an assistant inside Trivy itself. That is the adjacent MCP-server capability, not a built-in assistant, so it earns no credit here.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product
